title: PDF Captures ~70 Pyu Saw Htee Militia Members and Families in Pauk Township — 200+ Civilians Rescued from Kokkosu Village After Junta Militia Fled
detail: The Anyar Land Coalition (PDF alliance) confirmed on June 7, 2026 the capture of approximately 70 Pyu Saw Htee pro-junta militia members and family members in Pauk Township, Magway Region, following the PDF's capture of the Kukkosu (Kokkosu) militia camp during operations on June 2–4. The Anyar Land Coalition seized the Yay Pyar police station on June 2, then captured the Kukkosu Pyu Saw Htee militia camp on June 4, killing 40+ junta troops and militia, taking 20+ prisoners alive, and seizing 30+ weapons including a 60mm mortar. More than 200 civilians who had been trapped in Kokkosu village were freed and given medical care. The 70+ militia members captured — including elderly members in their 60s–70s and at least one man with a child — fled toward the Myaing Township border area before being intercepted. They are being held as prisoners of war; the militia leader and five others remained at large as of June 7. The operation in Pauk Township follows the PDF's May 26 liberation of a Pyu Saw Htee camp in Myaing Township (49 civilians rescued) and represents the sustained resistance dismantling of junta-aligned militia networks across the Magway-Sagaing corridor, where the PDF has been conducting a strategic attrition campaign against SAC infrastructure and proxy forces throughout 2026.

media.caption: PDF captures ~70 Pyu Saw Htee militia members and families near Pauk Township after Anyar Land Coalition overruns Kokkosu camp; 200+ civilians rescued, 40+ junta/militia killed.

title: Myanmar Junta Lashes Out at Timor-Leste President Over 'ASEAN Stain' Comment — SAC Foreign Ministry Condemns Ramos-Horta's Public Criticism
detail: Myanmar's military-controlled Foreign Ministry issued a sharp rebuke to Timor-Leste President José Ramos-Horta on June 6–7, 2026 after he publicly called Myanmar's civil war 'a stain on ASEAN's otherwise impressive catalogue of successes.' The SAC's Foreign Ministry statement dismissed Ramos-Horta's remarks as interference in Myanmar's internal affairs and rejected his characterization of the conflict. Timor-Leste is an ASEAN member state (acceded 2023) and Ramos-Horta — a Nobel Peace Laureate and veteran of Timor-Leste's independence struggle against Indonesian occupation — has been one of the most outspoken ASEAN leaders on Myanmar, pushing for stronger collective action from the bloc. The rebuke comes as the SAC works to consolidate international legitimacy following Min Aung Hlaing's India state visit (May 30–June 3) and FM Tin Maung Swe's Beijing visit (June 4–6). It also follows Min Aung Hlaing's exclusion from the ASEAN Leaders' Summit in Cebu (May 7, 2026 — only the Permanent Secretary attended) and his decision not to attend the ASEAN-Russia Summit in Kazan (June 17–19, 2026; FM Than Swe attending in his place). The junta's diplomatic isolation within ASEAN — despite China's diplomatic endorsement — remains a significant constraint on its international legitimacy, particularly as the ongoing multi-front war produces increasingly documented atrocities.

media.caption: Myanmar junta's Foreign Ministry rebukes Timor-Leste President Ramos-Horta for calling Myanmar's civil war 'a stain on ASEAN' — diplomatic isolation continues despite India and China visits.

title: SAC Aircraft, Suicide Drones, and Artillery Strike Karenni State — Baptist Pastor Killed in Demoso, Hpruso, and Nanmekhon Area Attacks
detail: Junta aircraft, suicide drones, and artillery struck civilian areas in Demoso, Hpruso, and Nanmekhon areas of Karenni (Kayah) State in late June 6–7, 2026, killing at least one Baptist pastor and injuring three civilians. The attacks targeted areas administered by the Karenni Nationalities Defence Force (KNDF) and allied resistance forces. The Baptist pastor was killed during the aerial bombardment — the latest in a series of attacks on religious clergy documented in Myanmar's civil war, following the killing of two monks in the Seik Hkun Monastery airstrike (April 13, 2026), a monk killed at the Shwebo IDP camp (April 7), and a monk killed in a Bhamo monastery strike (May 7). SAC suicide drones also struck Lay Taung Town in Ramree Township, Rakhine State on June 6. Karenni State has been under sustained SAC aerial campaign throughout 2026, with the KNDF and allied Karenni forces maintaining control of most rural territory while the junta uses its air power advantage against civilian areas it cannot hold on the ground. The KNDF and Karenni Army have successfully encircled the junta garrison in Loikaw — the state capital — which has been reduced to airlifts for resupply for over a year.

media.caption: SAC aircraft, suicide drones, and artillery strike Karenni State: Baptist pastor killed in Demoso/Hpruso/Nanmekhon attacks; separately, Ramree Township (Rakhine) also bombed June 6.
